reason: A trace with aria snapshots of each action. Trace.record has screenshots and DOM snapshots, not aria snapshots, so the matrix row's `has` covers only the options it does take
The requests of an APIRequestContext (`context.request`, `page.request`, or a request context of the test's own), which Strider has no counterpart of, recorded in a trace of their own
Naming a trace's chunks and writing them to a traces directory on disk, as `tracesDir` and `name` do; Strider exports a recording to the path given to exportTrace
Chunks within one running trace, each exported on its own and keeping only its own resources. Strider's recordings are independent scopes, with no rollover inside one
A wait that spans two chunks, with its end left out of the second: Strider has no chunks, so one recording holds the whole wait
Frames scaled to fit, crop, or scale within a size, as Playwright's screencast does; Strider's screencast frames keep the page's own size, with no size option

Two chunks of one trace saved while a WebSocket streams, each with its own WebSocket frames (a `.jsonl` resource). Strider has no chunks, and `Trace.record` writes its network entries without WebSocket frames; the fixture server has no WebSocket endpoint either
Playwright's internal stack session directory (`_stacksId`), which a failed save must release. Strider keeps no such directory: a recording's steps are in memory until its export
Reads the trace file Playwright's test runner writes to its traces directory while tracing runs. Strider writes no file until an export, so there is no file to read
Stopping a trace that was never started: a Strider recording exists only once `Trace.record` has started it, so there is no stop to call before a start, and the type has no such state

Playwright's disposable returned by start and startChunk, which discards the trace so that a later stop throws. A Strider recording has no discard that makes its export fail: `remove` ends it, and `exportTrace` still writes what it recorded
